```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

library(tidyverse)
```

# Part 1: Factors That Influence Employee Attrition

## 1. Import and Prepare Data

```{r}
employee <- read_csv(
  "../data/week13_employee.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

employee <- employee %>%
  mutate(
    Attrition = factor(
      Attrition,
      levels = c("Yes", "No")
    )
  )

glimpse(employee)
```

## 2. Data Checks

```{r}
# Number of rows and columns
dim(employee)

# Missing values
sum(is.na(employee))

# Duplicated rows
sum(duplicated(employee))

# Variables with only one unique value
employee %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), n_distinct)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Unique_values"
  ) %>%
  filter(Unique_values <= 1)
```

## 3. Overall Attrition

```{r}
attrition_summary <- employee %>%
  count(Attrition) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2)
  )

attrition_summary
```

```{r}
ggplot(employee, aes(x = Attrition, fill = Attrition)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Overall Employee Attrition",
    x = "Attrition",
    y = "Number of Employees"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## 4. Department and Attrition

```{r}
department_result <- employee %>%
  group_by(Department) %>%
  summarise(
    Employees = n(),
    Attrition_rate = round(
      mean(Attrition == "Yes") * 100,
      2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Attrition_rate))

department_result
```

```{r}
ggplot(employee, aes(x = Department, fill = Attrition)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Attrition by Department",
    x = "Department",
    y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 5. Business Travel and Attrition

```{r}
travel_result <- employee %>%
  group_by(BusinessTravel) %>%
  summarise(
    Employees = n(),
    Attrition_rate = round(
      mean(Attrition == "Yes") * 100,
      2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Attrition_rate))

travel_result
```

```{r}
ggplot(employee, aes(x = BusinessTravel, fill = Attrition)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Attrition by Business Travel",
    x = "Business Travel",
    y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 6. Age and Years at Company

```{r}
employee %>%
  group_by(Attrition) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_age = round(mean(Age), 2),
    Mean_years_at_company =
      round(mean(YearsAtCompany), 2)
  )
```

```{r}
employee %>%
  select(
    Attrition,
    Age,
    YearsAtCompany
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -Attrition,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x = Attrition, y = Value, fill = Attrition)
  ) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(
    ~Variable,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Age and Years at Company by Attrition",
    x = "Attrition",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## 7. Preliminary Findings

```{r echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
overall_rate <- round(
  mean(employee$Attrition == "Yes") * 100,
  2
)

top_department <- department_result[1, ]
top_travel <- travel_result[1, ]

cat(
  paste0(
    "- The overall attrition rate was **",
    overall_rate,
    "%**.\n\n",
    "- **",
    top_department$Department,
    "** had the highest department attrition rate.\n\n",
    "- **",
    top_travel$BusinessTravel,
    "** had the highest attrition rate among the business travel groups.\n\n",
    "- Age and years at the company also showed differences between employees who left and employees who stayed.\n\n",
    "- These results show associations and do not prove causal relationships."
  )
)
```
